narrative.overview:
A dark, precise working surface where the shipped work is the hero, dressed in the brand kit's colours. The world is dark only (`color-scheme: dark`): the kit's black ground, warm off-white ink, neutral labels, and the kit's orange as the only colour, with a job every time it appears. The interface steps back so real screenshots of live client sites carry the page: they are dealt as a 3D deck in the hero, and they sit in hairline frames on every project card. Nothing on the surface is illustration; the imagery is the evidence, and the screenshots bring the colour the interface withholds.

The register is calm, exact, and workmanlike. Headings are Schibsted Grotesk, tight and heavy at 700–800; running text is Instrument Sans; every piece of data (stacks, context tags, hostnames, form labels, button labels) speaks in uppercase DM Mono. Depth is tonal: ground to surface to second surface, one step at a time, drawn with 1px hairlines and no glow. The exception is physical layering: a phone capture laid over a desktop screenshot, screenshots stacked in the hero deck, and the portrait badge hanging on its strap each cast a soft shadow, because they really sit on top of something.

Density is generous and editorial: a centered 72rem column, wide vertical rhythm, sections divided by full-width hairlines, lists divided by hairlines instead of boxed into cards. Effects stay alive against that restraint as a stated exception: a field of neutral mono glyphs with a trace of orange flowing behind the hero, a name that decodes itself under an orange caret, screenshots dealt and re-shuffled as a deck, a crosshair that measures the contact page. Each page gets its own effects rather than one global trick. Effects are welcome and meant to show craft, but they are opt-out and always drawn from the palette. The world still refuses rainbow neon, candy accents, and the generic Swiss-Helvetica grid it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Kit black, dark only (`color-scheme: dark`), warm off-white ink.
Real screenshots of shipped sites are the imagery; no placeholders, no illustration.
One colour, the kit's orange, with a named list of jobs: never a section background, never under white text, never body text.
Neutral labels: mono labels are muted, and status has its own green and red.
Three voices: Schibsted Grotesk (headings), Instrument Sans (running text), DM Mono (all data/labels).
Depth by tonal step + hairlines; no glows or coloured shadows on the interface; soft shadows only where something physically sits on something else.
Expressive light and motion (shaders, glyph fields, type reveals, 3D decks) as an opt-out, palette-tinted exception, chosen per page.

rules.name: The Orange Job Rule
rules.body: Orange appears only for a job: the logo ring, the main button (one per screen, black text), link underlines and link text on hover, focus rings and selection, one emphasised word in a headline at most, the "live" hostname line. It is never a section background, never under white text, never body text, never beside error red as a second accent, and never decoration with no job. If you cannot name the job, use a neutral.

rules.name: The Neutral Label Rule
rules.body: Mono labels are muted, not coloured. A hostname line is the one label that is orange, because orange there means the site is live: "coming soon" and NDA lines stay muted, so the colour carries information.

rules.name: The Context Mark Rule
rules.body: How a project came about is shown by who it was with, never a colour wash: Freelance is a 0.4rem `currentColor` dot plus the word; macmac and Marvelous Digital appear as their own wordmarks, monochrome in `currentColor` (`ContextBadge.astro`, SVGs in `src/components/icons/`), with the name as screen-reader text. Sizes: 0.62rem (macmac) / 0.92rem (Marvelous) in caption lines and chips, ~1.4/1.9rem on the About page. Never recolour or restyle the partner wordmarks.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Headings are Schibsted Grotesk; prose is Instrument Sans; anything that reads as data (labels, stacks, tags, hostnames, buttons) is DM Mono, uppercase, tracked. A voice never crosses into another's job.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No mono kicker or label sits above a section heading; mono labels only name data next to it (a `dt` beside its `dd`, a context tag above a card title that it describes).

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by a 1px `line` border and one tonal step, never by a shadow. A shadow only ever marks a literal physical overlap: something resting on, or hanging in front of, something else.

rules.name: The Screenshots Carry The Colour Rule
rules.body: The interface has no glows and no coloured shadows. Colour and richness come from the screenshots; if a surface needs more presence, give the work more room rather than the chrome more light.

rules.name: The Effects Exception Rule
rules.body: Effects keep expressive light and motion, including glow, as a stated exception to the no-glow rule, because they are opt-out, palette-tinted moments. The exception covers `src/components/islands/fx/` only; static interface elements never inherit it.

dos: Do let real screenshots of shipped sites be the imagery; crop them to 16:10 (desktop) or 390:844 (phone), top-anchored, inside a hairline frame.

Do give orange a job: the logo ring, the main button (one per screen, black text), link underlines and link text on hover, focus rings and selection, one emphasised word in a headline at most, the "live" hostname line.
Do keep mono labels muted, and report state with `success` and `error`, not orange.
Do show project context with the ContextBadge (freelance dot or partner wordmark) wherever context appears.
Do step depth one tone at a time (ground, `surface`, `surface-2`), separate surfaces with the `line` hairline, and divide lists with hairlines instead of boxing them into cards.
Do put all data (stacks, tags, hostnames, labels, buttons) in DM Mono, uppercase, tracked.
Do draw icons as inline SVG strokes (1.5px, square caps) sized in `em`.

Do gate every animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` with an intentional still alternative, give long-running content motion a pause control, and stop loops and shaders when off-screen or the tab is hidden.
Do tint every effect from the palette through tokens: orange for small interaction moments; neutral `LIGHT` with `ACCENT` as a trace (the `accent` param) for shader backgrounds.
Do keep content in the HTML and visible without JS; effects decorate it (`aria-hidden` layers, a CSS failsafe for anything hidden before it animates).
Do ship every visitor-facing string in both EN and FR (binding product constraint).
donts: Don't use orange as a section background, under white text, as body text, beside error red as a second accent, or as decoration with no job; the closing CTA is a flat `surface` band with an orange button.
Don't add glows or coloured shadows to the interface; only opt-out effects may carry light.
Don't add drop shadows for elevation; shadows only mark physical layering (the phone capture, the hero deck, the hanging badge).
Don't use placeholder imagery or stock illustration in place of real work. The only portrait is Thomas's real photo (`src/assets/portrait.jpg`, About page).
Don't put a mono eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't use unicode glyph arrows (→ ↗) or emoji as icons.
Don't use off-palette glows, rainbow or saturated neon gradients, or a second bold accent.
Don't add a light theme; the world is dark only.
Don't recolour the logo's ring and peaks.
Don't run prose in the mono voice, or data in the prose voice.
Don't let an effect cut text contrast below AA, tint the screenshots themselves, or add heavy runtime dependencies when a small hand-written island does the job.
Don't add a further typeface or a system font; the three faces are fixed.
